question.problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{e}^{uv} \\ u+2v\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the locations of the critical points of $T,$ we need to solve 

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)={e}^{uv}$ and $y(u,v)=u+2v.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =v{e}^{uv} & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =u{e}^{uv} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}v{e}^{uv} & u{e}^{uv} \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =v{e}^{uv}\cdot 2-u{e}^{uv}\cdot 1 \\  & ={e}^{uv}(2v-u).\end{aligned}
$$

 

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.$ So, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =0 \\ {e}^{uv}(2v-u) & =0 \\ 2v-u & =0 \\ u & =2v.\end{aligned}
$$

  

The equation $u=2v$ defines a line in the $uv$-plane.

choices.value: The critical points lie on the line $u=2v.$
The critical points lie on the hyperbola $uv=\operatorname{ln}⁡2.$
The critical points lie on the line $u=-2v.$
The critical points lie on the line $v=2u.$
The critical points lie on the line $v=-2u.$
